description:
The tree was re-inspected on 23/09/2026 :
OBSERVATIONS:

Very slight lifting of the ground on the north side of the stem up to 2m from the base of the tree. No buttressing noted around the base of the tree. Stem growing on 10Â° lean to south, becoming more pronounced to a 15- 20Â° lean from 3m and stays at this angle past crown break overhanging single storey light construction classrooms below.  
Main stem bifurcation at 4.5m with larger (main) scaffold on northeast side and secondary scaffold on southwest side.  Secondary scaffold 1.5m from main bifurcation doglegs towards southwest at a sharp angle on top of this dogleg is an old pruning stub, approx. 30cm across. The scaffold then grows at a near horizontal angle before forming two upright stems. The underside of this proportion of the scaffold has a bark pattern consistent with reaction wood formation. On this same scaffold is a large pruning wound just after upright stems, woundwood present but exposed wood visible. 
Main scaffold trifurcates at 1.5m after main stem bifurcation, with all stems forming within 1m distance. The northern facing and central stem has been removed, the stub is still on the floor adjacent to the tree and was removed after structural failure. The other two stems grow horizontally for 1-2m before producing upright stems at sharp dogleg angles. The crown is overall significantly biased to the south. Multiple old pruning wounds throughout canopy. Needles appear healthy and a dense volume of cones are forming throughout the crown.  The removal of the northern branch has left the tree with a very unbalanced appearance.  

RECOMMENDATION AND REASONS FOR PROPOSED WORKS

The tree has multiple defects from historic poor pruning and is significantly weighted with a considerable lean over the single storey classroom to the south below. Given the intense usage of the site as a primary school with the permanent target of the low level classroom of light construction and the high frequency usage of the school playground the tree is considered to pose an unacceptably high risk to the school with a high probabllity of either large limb failure or whole tree failure, therefore removal and replacement is recommended.
